reason: The text contains the named character Uriah the Hittite (אוּרִיָּה הַחִתִּי), who is presented as a soldier and servant in David's military. While he plays a significant role in the narrative, he is essentially a regular military person—a soldier with no exceptional political, religious, or royal status. Unlike David (king), Joab (military commander), and Nathan (prophet), Uriah represents an ordinary person whose profession is military service.
